purpose: Author-checked development rows for post-vote fidelity and peer-attribution calibration. None is a prospective prediction example or a held-out case.

facts: Both France and China voted for amendment S/2025/116.
Amendment S/2025/116 received 11 in favour, one against and three abstentions. The negative vote by a permanent member prevented adoption.
The Council adopted the underlying draft S/2025/112 as resolution 2774 with ten in favour, none against and five abstentions. China voted yes. France abstained.
France said it sought a just and lasting peace grounded in the Charter and respect for Ukrainian sovereignty, territorial integrity and independence.
cases.accurate_peer: France and China voted together on S/2025/116. The permanent-member veto kept that amendment out of the adopted text.
cases.unsupported_peer: France and China both voted for amendment S/2025/116, so we can say both endorsed the adopted United States draft and its incorporated amendment.
cases.critical_error: Treating an amendment vote as approval of the ultimate draft, or describing the vetoed amendment as incorporated.

cases.meeting: S/PV.9214, 9 December 2022, roll call and Indian national statement
facts: The Council adopted the humanitarian exemption draft 14–0–1. Brazil voted yes and India abstained.
In its national statement, India said it had sought a proactive 1267 Monitoring Team role with robust reporting and that those concerns were not fully addressed.
India distinguished prospective review of implementation from what had already entered the adopted text.
cases.accurate_peer: The draft passed, and India's abstention and its unresolved monitoring concerns should both appear in the record.
cases.unsupported_peer: The Council adopted the draft without an opposing vote. India therefore approved the text and confirmed the requested monitoring standard was incorporated.
cases.critical_error: Equating abstention with support or claiming that the adopted text fully satisfied India's request.

cases.meeting: S/PV.8514, 23 April 2019, France and UK post-vote statements
facts: France and the United Kingdom both supported the adopted resolution 2467 and objected to omissions about health services.
France explicitly included the choice to terminate involuntary pregnancies. The UK emphasized civil society and accountability alongside care.
The statements give evidence about their response to the 2019 text and their stated support for care.
cases.accurate_peer: The two governments supported the adopted text while objecting to omissions about care. Keep the distinct emphases attached to the speakers.
cases.unsupported_peer: Both delegations welcomed the text and therefore approved its omissions. We can attribute France's explicit wording on termination to the United Kingdom as well.
cases.critical_error: Equating support for the overall text with approval of its omissions, or pooling a French formulation into the UK's statement.
